+## #2861 - Example case 2d/slots: one block, a Slot and a Trochoidal slot
+
+**What was decided.** The case `examples/catalog/2d/slots` is a
+100 x 60 x 12 mm block with two closed slots along X. Each slot is 10 mm
+wide, 6 mm deep and 60 mm long. A Slot cuts the slot at `Y15`. A Trochoidal
+slot cuts the slot at `Y-15`. The two operations use the same 6 mm flat end
+mill, the same width and the same floor (`Z6`).
+
+- Slot: stepover 2 mm, stepdown 3 mm, `F600`. The levels are `Z9` and `Z6`.
+- Trochoidal slot: full depth in one level, `max_engagement` 60 degrees,
+  `step` 0.8 mm, microlift return of 0.3 mm, `F1200`.
+
+**Why.**
+
+- One part with the two slots lets a reader compare the two programs in one
+  file. Only the operation kind and its cutting data are different.
+- A 10 mm slot with a 6 mm tool leaves 2 mm of room on each side. The Slot
+  needs more than one row, and the Trochoidal slot has room for its loops.
+- Each operation uses the cutting data that is usual for it. The Slot cuts
+  with the full tool diameter, so it takes two levels at a low feed. The
+  Trochoidal slot keeps a small contact angle, so it takes the full depth at
+  two times the feed. The README table shows the result: 19 motion blocks
+  against 803, and 0.60 min against 1.28 min of feed moves.
+- The slots are closed and are inside the block. The gouge check then judges
+  each tool path against real walls on all sides.
+- The model is a mesh that the generator script writes. No outside geometry
+  is used (Clean-Room Protocol). The script checks that the mesh is
+  watertight and that the top area is correct.
+- The round ends of the model have 64 chords for each half circle. The
+  chords are inside the true circle by less than 0.002 mm. `verify` is ok
+  with the true 10 mm width.
+
+**Found during the work.** The Slot leaves up to 0.86 mm in its round ends,
+and `verify` is ok. The rows touch a round end only at their end points.
+#2906 is the bug. The README names it under "What to look at". The case
+keeps the 2 mm stepover, because it shows the behaviour clearly. A fix for
+#2906 changes `slots.nc`: rebuild the case with the fix.
+
+**Merge with main: the case tests are in the heavy lane.** Main now has
+one test module for each case (`catalog_<family>_<case>`), with a 60 s
+budget for each test. The module `catalog_2d_slots` takes about 40 s for
+each test in debug when it runs alone. In the parallel suite, it went over
+its budget. It also pushed `turning/cone-thread` over its budget. The two
+tests of `catalog_2d_slots` are `#[ignore]`d with a heavy-lane reason. The
+budget message tells the author to do this. `cargo xtask gate heavy` runs
+them in release. The default suite keeps
+`slots_case_posts_a_slot_and_a_trochoidal_slot_to_the_same_floor`, which
+reads the committed program. Dropped: a smaller model (it changes the
+committed program), and a larger budget (it changes a rule of main).
+
+**Considered and dropped.**
+
+- Two parts or two cases, one for each operation. The comparison needs the
+  two programs side by side.
+- Slots open at the two ends of the block. The end points are then outside
+  the block. This was not tried: a closed slot is the plain job, and its
+  round ends show the difference between the two operations.
+- The same stepdown and feed for the two operations. A Trochoidal slot at a
+  3 mm depth and `F600` does not show why a user selects it.
+- A smaller stepover for the Slot to make the leftover in the round ends
+  small. The leftover does not go to zero, and the example would hide #2906.
+- A check of the embedded mesh for this case in the two catalog tests. The
+  check for `2d/contour-tabs` pins a review fix of that case. The script of
+  this case removes the model link in the same way.
+
+**Cost to change later.** Small. Change `build.camscript`, run
+`cargo xtask catalog --case 2d/slots`, and update the test
+`slots_case_posts_a_slot_and_a_trochoidal_slot_to_the_same_floor` and the
+README table.
+
+**Pinned by.** `crates/app/tests/example_catalog.rs`:
+`slots_case_posts_a_slot_and_a_trochoidal_slot_to_the_same_floor`, and the
+two catalog tests that read each case.

+# Slots (Slot, Trochoidal slot)
+
+A 100 x 60 x 12 mm clean-room block with two closed slots along X. Each slot is 10 mm wide, 6 mm deep and 60 mm long, with round ends. A Slot cuts the slot at `Y15`. A Trochoidal slot cuts the slot at `Y-15`. The two operations use the same 6 mm tool, the same width and the same floor.
+
+## What it shows
+
+1. **Slot (`Slot1`, `EM-0600-4FL`):** Cuts the slot from `a` (`X-25 Y15`) to `b` (`X25 Y15`) in rows parallel to the centre line. The stepover is 2 mm, so each level has three rows: `Y13`, `Y15` and `Y17`. The stepdown is 3 mm, so the levels are `Z9` and `Z6` (the slot floor). The tool plunges straight down at the start of each level.
+2. **Trochoidal slot (`Trochoidal slot1`, `EM-0600-4FL`):** Cuts the slot from `a` (`X-25 Y-15`) to `b` (`X25 Y-15`) in loops at the full depth. The tool goes down to `Z6` on a helix around `a`. Then it makes 113 loops. Each loop cuts forward on a `G03` arc and comes back 0.3 mm above the floor (`return: "microlift"`). The last move is a half circle around `b`.
+
+## The two programs
+
+| | Slot | Trochoidal slot |
+|---|---|---|
+| Motion blocks | 19 | 803 |
+| Arc blocks (`G02`, `G03`) | 0 | 459 |
+| Cut levels | `Z9`, `Z6` | `Z6` only |
+| Depth of cut | 3 mm | 6 mm |
+| Cutting feed | `F600` | `F1200` |
+| Length of the feed moves | 329 mm | 1455 mm |
+| Time of the feed moves | 0.60 min | 1.28 min |
+
+- The Slot program is short. The row at `Y15` cuts with the full tool diameter in the material. That is why its depth of cut and its feed are small.
+- The Trochoidal slot program is 42 times longer. Each loop cuts only a thin crescent. `max_engagement: 60.0` keeps the contact angle at or below 60 degrees. That is why it can cut the full depth at two times the feed.
+- `step: 0.8` is the largest step that the planner can use. The posted step is 0.44 mm, because the engagement limit is the tighter limit.
+
+## What to look at
+
+- In `slots.nc`, the Slot has no arc block. The moves between two rows are straight lines, for example `G01 X27. Y15. Z9.` after the row at `Y13`.
+- The Slot leaves material in its round ends: at most 0.86 mm, on the wall at 45 degrees. The rows touch the round end only at their end points. `verify` does not report this. #2906 is the bug for it.
+- The Trochoidal slot starts with four `G03` blocks at `F150` that go down from `Z14` to `Z6`. This is the helix entry.
+- Each loop is the same group of seven blocks: one step along the wall at `Y-17`, two `G03` arcs at `Z6.` and `F1200`, one lift to `Z6.3`, two `G02` arcs back at `F2400`, and one move down to `Z6.` at `F150`.
+- The Trochoidal slot cuts its two round ends completely: a full circle around `a` and a half circle around `b`, each of 2 mm radius.
+- The model has flat chords on the round ends (64 for each half circle). The chords are inside the true 10 mm circle by less than 0.002 mm.
+
+## Files
+
+- `model/gen_slots_obj.py` — generator for the block and its two slots, with a watertight check and an area check.
+- `model/slots.obj` — generated mesh imported by `build.camscript`.
+- `build.camscript` — headless script building `slots.camproj` and posting `slots.nc` through CamCraft's undoable commands.
+- `slots.camproj` — committed project with the two generated toolpaths.
+- `slots.nc` — committed Fanuc NC program verified byte-for-byte in `crates/app/tests/example_catalog.rs`.
+
+## Rebuild and verify
+
+From the repository root:
+
+```sh
+cargo xtask catalog --case 2d/slots
+cargo test -p camcraft-app --test example_catalog
+```

+// Example catalog case: 2d/slots (#2392, #2861).
+// Builds slots.camproj and posts slots.nc headlessly through CamCraft's
+// undoable command verbs. Run with CWD = this case directory:
+//   camcraft-cli script build.camscript
+
+cam.import("model/slots.obj", "slots");
+// Keep the mesh in the project without a link to the script working directory.
+cam.call("set_model_link", { model: "slots", path: null });
+
+cam.call("set_stock", {
+  box: { dx: 100.0, dy: 60.0, dz: 12.0 }
+});
+
+cam.call("add_tool", { catalog: "EM-0600-4FL", holder: "none" });
+
+// The slot at y = 15: concentric passes at two levels.
+cam.call("add_operation", {
+  kind: "Slot",
+  name: "Slot1",
+  tool: "EM-0600-4FL",
+  source: "slots",
+  params: {
+    a: [-25.0, 15.0],
+    b: [25.0, 15.0],
+    width: 10.0,
+    stock_to_leave: 0.0,
+    clearance_z: { reference: "top_of_stock", offset: 15.0 },
+    retract_z: { reference: "top_of_stock", offset: 5.0 },
+    top_z: { reference: "top_of_stock", offset: 0.0 },
+    bottom_z: { reference: "top_of_stock", offset: -6.0 },
+    stepdown: 3.0,
+    stepover: 2.0,
+    feed: 600.0,
+    plunge_feed: 150.0,
+    climb: true
+  }
+});
+
+// The slot at y = -15: the same width, trochoid loops at the full depth.
+cam.call("add_operation", {
+  kind: "Trochoidal slot",
+  name: "Trochoidal slot1",
+  tool: "EM-0600-4FL",
+  source: "slots",
+  params: {
+    a: [-25.0, -15.0],
+    b: [25.0, -15.0],
+    width: 10.0,
+    step: 0.8,
+    max_engagement: 60.0,
+    "return": "microlift",
+    lift: 0.3,
+    smoothing: 0.5,
+    stock_to_leave: 0.0,
+    clearance_z: { reference: "top_of_stock", offset: 15.0 },
+    retract_z: { reference: "top_of_stock", offset: 5.0 },
+    top_z: { reference: "top_of_stock", offset: 0.0 },
+    bottom_z: { reference: "top_of_stock", offset: -6.0 },
+    stepdown: 6.0,
+    feed: 1200.0,
+    return_feed: 2400.0,
+    plunge_feed: 150.0,
+    climb: true
+  }
+});
+
+cam.generate();
+var verdict = cam.verify();
+if (!verdict.ok) {
+  throw new Error("catalog verify failed: " + JSON.stringify(verdict));
+}
+cam.save("slots.camproj");
+cam.post({ to: "slots.nc" });
+cam.report();

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Regenerate slots.obj, the model of the catalog case 2d/slots.
+
+The part is a clean-room Camcraft fixture: a 100 x 60 x 12 mm block, centred
+on the XY origin, z from 0 to 12. It has two closed slots along X. Each slot
+is 10 mm wide and 6 mm deep, with round ends. The centre line of each slot
+goes from x = -25 to x = 25. One slot is at y = 15 and one is at y = -15.
+
+Method: the top and the bottom of the block use one grid of lines in X and
+in Y. A grid cell is a quad, a round slot end, or the open middle of a slot.
+A round end is two fans of triangles from the two outer corners of its cell
+to the arc. The arc touches the next cell at one point, and that cell is a
+fan from the point. The slot floor is a triangle fan (the outline is convex). Each wall
+is one quad for each outline edge. All faces share the grid corners and the
+arc points, so the mesh has no T-junctions. The script checks that the mesh
+is watertight and consistently oriented, and that the top area is correct,
+before it writes the file.
+
+The arc points are on the true circle. The chords are inside the circle by
+less than 0.002 mm (64 chords for each half circle).
+
+Usage: python gen_slots_obj.py [output.obj]
+"""
+
+import math
+import sys
+
+HALF_X = 50.0
+HALF_Y = 30.0
+Z_BOTTOM = 0.0
+Z_FLOOR = 6.0
+Z_TOP = 12.0
+SLOT_HALF_LENGTH = 25.0   # the centre line goes from -25 to 25
+SLOT_RADIUS = 5.0         # the slot is 10 mm wide
+SLOT_Y = 15.0             # the two centre lines are at y = 15 and y = -15
+ARC_CHORDS = 64           # chords for each half circle; an even number
+
+XS = [-HALF_X, -SLOT_HALF_LENGTH - SLOT_RADIUS, -SLOT_HALF_LENGTH,
+      SLOT_HALF_LENGTH, SLOT_HALF_LENGTH + SLOT_RADIUS, HALF_X]
+YS = [-HALF_Y, -SLOT_Y - SLOT_RADIUS, -SLOT_Y + SLOT_RADIUS,
+      SLOT_Y - SLOT_RADIUS, SLOT_Y + SLOT_RADIUS, HALF_Y]
+SLOT_ROWS = {1: -SLOT_Y, 3: SLOT_Y}   # grid row -> y of the slot centre line
+
+
+def arc(cx, cy, start_deg):
+    """The points of a half circle, counter-clockwise from start_deg. The
+    first and the last point are exact grid corners."""
+    pts = []
+    for i in range(ARC_CHORDS + 1):
+        if i == 0 or i == ARC_CHORDS or 2 * i == ARC_CHORDS:
+            quarter = (start_deg + 90 * (2 * i // ARC_CHORDS)) % 360
+            dx, dy = {0: (1, 0), 90: (0, 1), 180: (-1, 0), 270: (0, -1)}[quarter]
+        else:
+            t = math.radians(start_deg + 180.0 * i / ARC_CHORDS)
+            dx, dy = math.cos(t), math.sin(t)
+        pts.append((cx + SLOT_RADIUS * dx, cy + SLOT_RADIUS * dy))
+    return pts
+
+
+def build():
+    faces = []
+    top_area = 0.0
+    for row in range(5):
+        y0, y1 = YS[row], YS[row + 1]
+        for col in range(5):
+            x0, x1 = XS[col], XS[col + 1]
+            # The bottom of the block: one quad for each cell, normal -Z.
+            faces.append([(x0, y0, Z_BOTTOM), (x0, y1, Z_BOTTOM),
+                          (x1, y1, Z_BOTTOM), (x1, y0, Z_BOTTOM)])
+            if row in SLOT_ROWS and col in (1, 2, 3):
+                continue
+            top_area += (x1 - x0) * (y1 - y0)
+            if row in SLOT_ROWS:
+                # A round end touches this cell at one point. The cell is a
+                # fan from that point, so the point is a corner of each face.
+                cy = SLOT_ROWS[row]
+                if col == 4:
+                    ring = [(x0, cy), (x0, y0), (x1, y0), (x1, y1), (x0, y1)]
+                else:
+                    ring = [(x1, cy), (x1, y1), (x0, y1), (x0, y0), (x1, y0)]
+                for i in range(1, 4):
+                    faces.append([(x, y, Z_TOP) for x, y in
+                                  (ring[0], ring[i], ring[i + 1])])
+                continue
+            faces.append([(x0, y0, Z_TOP), (x1, y0, Z_TOP),
+                          (x1, y1, Z_TOP), (x0, y1, Z_TOP)])
+
+    for row, cy in SLOT_ROWS.items():
+        y0, y1 = YS[row], YS[row + 1]
+        right = arc(SLOT_HALF_LENGTH, cy, 270)    # bottom -> right -> top
+        left = arc(-SLOT_HALF_LENGTH, cy, 90)     # top -> left -> bottom
+        half = ARC_CHORDS // 2
+        # The top of the block around each round end, normal +Z.
+        for pts, first, second in (
+            (right, (XS[4], y0), (XS[4], y1)),
+            (left, (XS[1], y1), (XS[1], y0)),
+        ):
+            tris = [[first, pts[i + 1], pts[i]] for i in range(half)]
+            tris += [[second, pts[i + 1], pts[i]] for i in range(half, ARC_CHORDS)]
+            for tri in tris:
+                top_area += area2(tri) / 2.0
+                faces.append([(x, y, Z_TOP) for x, y in tri])
+        # The slot outline, counter-clockwise seen from +Z.
+        outline = right + left
+        n = len(outline)
+        for i in range(1, n - 1):                 # the floor, normal +Z
+            faces.append([(x, y, Z_FLOOR) for x, y in
+                          (outline[0], outline[i], outline[i + 1])])
+        for i in range(n):                        # the walls, normal into the slot
+            (ax, ay), (bx, by) = outline[i], outline[(i + 1) % n]
+            faces.append([(bx, by, Z_FLOOR), (ax, ay, Z_FLOOR),
+                          (ax, ay, Z_TOP), (bx, by, Z_TOP)])
+
+    # The four sides of the block: one quad for each grid edge, normal outward.
+    for i in range(5):
+        x0, x1 = XS[i], XS[i + 1]
+        y0, y1 = YS[i], YS[i + 1]
+        faces.append([(x0, -HALF_Y, Z_BOTTOM), (x1, -HALF_Y, Z_BOTTOM),
+                      (x1, -HALF_Y, Z_TOP), (x0, -HALF_Y, Z_TOP)])
+        faces.append([(x1, HALF_Y, Z_BOTTOM), (x0, HALF_Y, Z_BOTTOM),
+                      (x0, HALF_Y, Z_TOP), (x1, HALF_Y, Z_TOP)])
+        faces.append([(HALF_X, y0, Z_BOTTOM), (HALF_X, y1, Z_BOTTOM),
+                      (HALF_X, y1, Z_TOP), (HALF_X, y0, Z_TOP)])
+        faces.append([(-HALF_X, y1, Z_BOTTOM), (-HALF_X, y0, Z_BOTTOM),
+                      (-HALF_X, y0, Z_TOP), (-HALF_X, y1, Z_TOP)])
+    return faces, top_area
+
+
+def area2(tri):
+    """Two times the signed area of a 2D triangle (positive: counter-clockwise)."""
+    (ax, ay), (bx, by), (cx, cy) = tri
+    return (bx - ax) * (cy - ay) - (cx - ax) * (by - ay)
+
+
+def check(faces, top_area):
+    """Watertight and consistently oriented: every directed edge appears
+    exactly once and its reverse appears exactly once. The top area is the
+    block area minus the two slot outlines."""
+    seen = set()
+    for face in faces:
+        for p, q in zip(face, face[1:] + face[:1]):
+            if p == q:
+                raise SystemExit("degenerate face: %r" % (face,))
+            if (p, q) in seen:
+                raise SystemExit("directed edge reused: %r -> %r" % (p, q))
+            seen.add((p, q))
+    for (p, q) in seen:
+        if (q, p) not in seen:
+            raise SystemExit("open edge: %r -> %r" % (p, q))
+
+    step = math.pi / ARC_CHORDS
+    half_disc = ARC_CHORDS * 0.5 * SLOT_RADIUS ** 2 * math.sin(step)
+    slot = 2.0 * SLOT_HALF_LENGTH * 2.0 * SLOT_RADIUS + 2.0 * half_disc
+    want = 4.0 * HALF_X * HALF_Y - 2.0 * slot
+    if abs(top_area - want) > 1e-6:
+        raise SystemExit("top area %.9f, expected %.9f" % (top_area, want))
+
+
+def main():
+    out = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "slots.obj"
+    faces, top_area = build()
+    check(faces, top_area)
+
+    vid = {}
+    vlines = []
+    for face in faces:
+        for p in face:
+            if p not in vid:
+                vid[p] = len(vlines) + 1
+                vlines.append("v %.9g %.9g %.9g" % p)
+    flines = ["f " + " ".join(str(vid[p]) for p in face) for face in faces]
+
+    with open(out, "w") as fh:
+        fh.write(HEADER)
+        fh.write("\n" + "\n".join(vlines) + "\n\n" + "\n".join(flines) + "\n")
+    print("wrote %s: %d vertices, %d faces" % (out, len(vlines), len(flines)))
+
+
+HEADER = """\
+# Camcraft example catalog, case 2d/slots: a 100 x 60 x 12 mm block with two
+# closed slots along X, each 10 mm wide and 6 mm deep, centred on the XY
+# origin, z 0 to 12.
+# Authored for this repository (clean-room fixture); generated by
+# gen_slots_obj.py as a watertight mesh."""
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()
